import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 755

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/755](https://www.erdosproblems.com/755)
- [ErPu75] Erdős, Paul and Purdy, George, Some extremal problems in geometry. III.
  (1975), 291--308.
- [Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and
  combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261--269.
- [CDL25b] Clemen, Felix Christian, Dumitrescu, Adrian, and Liu, Dingyuan,
  The number of regular simplices in higher dimensions. arXiv:2507.19841 (2025).
-/

open Filter Metric
open scoped EuclideanGeometry Asymptotics

namespace Erdos755

/-- A three-point set whose pairwise distances are all equal to `side`. -/
def IsEquilateralTriangle {d : ℕ} (side : ℝ)
    (T : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  T.card = 3 ∧ ∀ p ∈ T, ∀ q ∈ T, p ≠ q → dist p q = side

/-- A unit equilateral triangle in Euclidean `d`-space. -/
def IsUnitEquilateralTriangle {d : ℕ}
    (T : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  IsEquilateralTriangle 1 T

/-- An equilateral triangle of any positive side length in Euclidean `d`-space. -/
def IsAnySizeEquilateralTriangle {d : ℕ}
    (T : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  ∃ side : ℝ, 0 < side ∧ IsEquilateralTriangle side T

/-- Number of unit equilateral triangles spanned by a finite point set. -/
noncomputable def unitEquilateralTriangleCount (d : ℕ)
    (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  ((P.powersetCard 3).filter fun T => IsUnitEquilateralTriangle T).card

/-- Number of equilateral triangles of any positive side length spanned by a finite point set. -/
noncomputable def anySizeEquilateralTriangleCount (d : ℕ)
    (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  ((P.powersetCard 3).filter fun T => IsAnySizeEquilateralTriangle T).card

/-- Maximum number of unit equilateral triangles spanned by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. -/
noncomputable def TUnit (d n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m : ℕ | ∃ P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    P.card = n ∧ unitEquilateralTriangleCount d P = m}

/-- Maximum number of equilateral triangles of any size spanned by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. -/
noncomputable def TAnySize (d n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {m : ℕ | ∃ P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
    P.card = n ∧ anySizeEquilateralTriangleCount d P = m}

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_755.test_dim_one :
    unitEquilateralTriangleCount 1 (∅ : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))) = 0 := by
  simp [unitEquilateralTriangleCount]

/--
Erdős asked whether every $n$-point set in
$\mathbb{R}^6$ spans at most $(1/27 + o(1)) n^3$ unit equilateral triangles.

Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger any-size statement
$T_6(n) = (1/27 + o(1)) n^3$. The unit-triangle upper bound follows as a
corollary, since unit equilateral triangles are a subset of equilateral
triangles of any positive side length: $T_\mathrm{unit} \leq T_\mathrm{anysize}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos755.lean#L1344"]
theorem erdos_755 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ,
      o =o[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ => (1 : ℝ)) ∧
        ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
          (TUnit 6 n : ℝ) ≤ ((1 / 27 : ℝ) + o n) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu [CDL25b] proved the stronger version where
equilateral triangles of all positive side lengths are counted.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_755.variants.any_size_cdl :
    (fun n : ℕ => (TAnySize 6 n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (1 / 27 : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 3) := by
  sorry

end Erdos755

reformulations.difference: The unit-triangle upper bound is encoded using a supremal counting function and an existential little-o error, rather than a uniform epsilon bound over all finite point configurations.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The attainable counts are nonempty in dimension 6 and bounded by n.choose 3, so their natural-number supremum is an attained maximum. The Lean statement is therefore equivalent to: for every ε > 0, there exists N such that every n-point configuration with n ≥ N spans at most (1/27 + ε)n³ unit triangles. The reverse analytic implication uses o(n) = max(TUnit(6,n)/n³ - 1/27, 0) for positive n. The complete equivalence was proved as Review755.main_epsilon_all_sets. This verifies the asymptotic encoding, separately from the historical wording limitation below.

reformulations.difference: The source gives T₆(n) = n³/27 + o(n³); Lean uses asymptotic equivalence to n³/27.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Theorem 2 of the cited paper, specialized to d = 6 and k = 3, has leading coefficient binomial(3,3)/3³ = 1/27. Since this coefficient is nonzero, asymptotic equivalence to n³/27 is equivalent to an eventually exact representation T₆(n) = (1/27 + o(n))n³ with o(n) → 0. The n = 0 denominator issue is irrelevant at atTop. This equivalence was proved as Review755.anysize_additive_reformulation.

could_not_verify: Erdos755.erdos_755 — exact original wording and historical attribution: erdosproblems.com/755 and its bibliography remained Cloudflare-blocked despite descriptive User-Agent headers, and I could not locate the 1994 primary paper [Er94b]. CDL v4 attributes an arbitrary-size conjecture to Erdős, whereas the file's main declaration is unit-only. Without the original/web wording, I cannot finally settle that distinction; it is not reported as a defect. The unit bound itself and its cited formal proof were verified, and the file's any-size variant faithfully states CDL's result.
review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defects were found. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify positivity of triangle side lengths, counting bounds and attained maxima, zero counts for fewer than three points, TUnit 6 3 = TAnySize 6 3 = 1, and the implication from the any-size result to the unit bound. The cited external proof compiled successfully; its main theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The solved tags and positive answer are supported by the paper and status metadata. The reviewed file remains byte-identical to the specified commit.
